newsitem.title: UK: UK's ITC says "Monarchy" TV debate broke no codes.
newsitem.headline: UK's ITC says "Monarchy" TV debate broke no codes.

text.p: A television programme that debated the future of the British monarchy was not "a programme of high quality", but did not breach codes on impartiality, a British television watchdog said on Monday.
The Independent Television Commission (ITC) said 53 viewers complained about the style and content of the programme, "Monarchy - The Nation Decides".
Another 32 viewers complained because they were unable to register their votes in a telephone poll conducted in conjunction with the show.
The programme, broadcast in January by ITV licensee Carlton Communications, featured a panel debate and contributions from an audience of 3,000, as well as the telephone poll.

"The ITC recognised that 'Monarchy' brought a new format to peak-time current affairs output on ITV and was distinctive and in certain respects innovative," the ITC said in a monthly report on complaints about television programmes and advertising.
"However, the ITC also explained to Carlton that this could not be regarded as a programme of high quality," it said.
The ITC, however, said the programme breached no codes.
